threads.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, objectives, and roles before detailed planning starts.

messages.text: Morning all. Kicking off this channel for the Integrated Youth Wellbeing and Outreach Pilot Programme. I have shared the Pilot Programme Overview and Objectives in A1 so we have a single reference for scope, outcomes, and constraints. For this thread, can we focus on two things: 1) confirming the target youth groups and locations for the pilot, linked to T1, and 2) being clear who is leading on outreach, workshops, and oral health sessions. Please have a look at A1 before replying and drop any questions or concerns here.

Thanks for starting this. From A1 and what we discussed informally, I understand the priority is at-risk youth already known to social services plus those flagged by schools. For T1, I can help map locations and travel times once we lock the list of schools and community spots. My initial thought is: main secondary school, alternative provision unit, youth drop-in centre, and the community sports hall. Are there any other locations we should consider before I start sketching this into T6 and A6 later?

I have gone through A1 and it looks aligned with what we see pastorally. From my side, I would suggest we explicitly include young carers and those with recent bereavement, as they often do not self-identify as at-risk but show up in pastoral conversations. They are usually in the main secondary school and the alternative provision. I am happy to support T1 by sharing a list of existing pastoral groups and lunchtime clubs where these young people already gather, if that helps refine the locations.

I have reviewed A1 as well. For T1, could we clarify whether we are including youth who are not currently in education, for example those who have dropped out or are on part-time timetables? If yes, we may need at least one community-based location that is not tied to school hours. That will also affect how we design the attendance and feedback templates in A3 and T4, because we might need slightly different fields for school-based versus community-based sessions.

From the oral health side, A1 mentions on-site awareness and screening. For T5, it would be most practical if we focus on locations where we can set up a small, clean corner with access to water or at least hand hygiene facilities. The main secondary school and the dental clinic are straightforward. The youth drop-in centre should be fine if we coordinate with the manager. The sports hall might be trickier unless there is a side room. I can check what is realistic with the dental clinic supervisor once we have a draft list.

On the question about youth not currently in education: my view is that they should be in scope, especially those already known to social services. Practically, that means we add the youth drop-in centre and possibly one more community venue, like the library or a community hub, to T1. We will need to check with the social services manager and community health coordinator before confirming. I can draft a short list of target groups and locations today and share it here for sign-off under D1.

That works for me. Once you share the draft list for T1, I will plug the locations into a simple routing plan for T6 and A6, with estimated travel times and some buffer. I will also note any obvious access or timing constraints, for example if the library has limited after-school slots. Before we call D1, could we agree how many locations we can realistically cover each week within existing staff hours?

On capacity, from a pastoral perspective I can reliably support one school-based workshop block per week plus one smaller group or drop-in. Anything beyond that might stretch the time needed for follow-up with individual students. For the wellbeing workshops linked to T3, I would prefer to keep them in the main secondary school and the alternative provision initially, and then add a community-based group only if attendance is strong and we can manage the follow-up.

If we keep to two main school locations plus one community site, that should be manageable from an admin side. For T4 and later T7, I can standardise the attendance and information materials so we are not reinventing forms for each place. It would help if, when you draft A6, you indicate which sessions are more outreach-focused versus more structured workshops, so we can align the templates and messaging.

From my rota, I can commit to one oral health awareness and screening block per week, either at a school or at the clinic, as part of T5. If we try to cover more than two different locations in a week for oral health, we may run into equipment and sterilisation constraints. So for D1 and D2, I would suggest we prioritise the main secondary school and the clinic for the first month, then review whether we can add the youth drop-in centre.

Here is a proposed list for T1, based on A1 and your inputs: 1) Main secondary school: focus on students with existing pastoral flags, young carers, and those with attendance issues. 2) Alternative provision unit: focus on students at risk of exclusion or already excluded. 3) Youth drop-in centre: focus on out-of-school youth and those on reduced timetables. 4) Dental clinic: for oral health awareness and screening, mainly referrals from the above groups. If there are no strong objections, I suggest we confirm these four as our pilot locations under D1.

No objections from me. The four locations you listed are workable, and I can build T6 and A6 around them. I will assume one visit per week to each school, plus a rotating slot between the youth drop-in centre and the clinic, unless the social services manager or school leadership advise otherwise. I will flag any clashes with school timetables once I have a first draft schedule.

I am comfortable with those four locations as well. For roles, my understanding is: I will lead on the wellbeing workshop curriculum and delivery at the main secondary school and alternative provision, linked to T3 and T9. I can also support one-to-one follow-up where needed. I will need some help coordinating with school leadership on room bookings and timings, which I can raise with the social services manager.

On roles, I can take the lead on T4 and T7: creating the attendance and feedback templates in line with A3, and compiling youth-facing information materials that match the workshop and oral health content in A4 and A5. I will also support with basic data entry where needed, but I will need clarity on who is responsible for reviewing participation trends week by week so that T10 is covered.

To summarise my role for D2: I will lead on planning and delivering the oral health awareness and screening sessions under T5 and T11, using A5 and A7 as references. That includes preparing materials, coordinating with the dental clinic supervisor for clinical sign-off, and keeping the inventory checklist up to date. I will also contribute to youth-facing materials where they touch on oral health, so they stay consistent with clinical guidelines.

Thanks all, this is shaping up clearly. For D2, here is what I propose we record: 1) I will lead on outreach mapping, case note system, and weekly participation monitoring under T1, T8, and T10, and coordinate with social services manager and youth reps. 2) Pastoral worker will lead on workshop curriculum and delivery under T3 and T9. 3) Dental chairside assistant will lead on oral health sessions and materials under T5 and T11. 4) Typist will lead on templates and youth-facing materials under T4 and T7. 5) Geology technician will lead on field visit schedule and routing under T6 and support T12 later. If there are no objections by tomorrow, I will treat this as agreed and share a short summary back to the social services manager.

No objections from me. Once you confirm D1 and D2 with the social services manager, please tag me so I can start drafting the templates in T4 and a simple summary of roles and locations to include at the top of A3. That way, anyone filling in attendance or feedback will see immediately which site and activity type they are recording.

All clear from my side as well. I will start a first pass of T6 and A6 using the four agreed locations under D1 and the role split under D2, and then we can refine once schools confirm preferred days.

threads.thread_goal: Define safeguarding, confidentiality, and record-keeping standards.

messages.text: I have put together a first draft of the safeguarding and confidentiality procedures for the pilot, linked to T2 and reflected in A2. It covers one-to-one and group settings, consent, information sharing, and how we handle disclosures during outreach, workshops, and oral health sessions. Before we ask the social services manager to review, could you please read through and share any gaps or practical concerns here?

Thanks for drafting this. I have read A2 and it is broadly in line with our existing child protection policy. A couple of points from the outreach side: 1) For T8, we need to be explicit that case notes and referral records will use anonymised IDs in any shared reports, and that only designated staff can link IDs to names. 2) For group outreach in community locations, we should clarify how we manage situations where a young person attends without a parent or carer and we do not have prior consent on file. I suggest we add a short section on verbal consent and information sheets for those cases.

I have gone through A2 with an eye on T4 and A3. To make the templates workable, we need to agree on the minimum data fields for each youth interaction under D4. My suggestion is: 1) unique ID, 2) age band, 3) location and type of session, 4) brief reason for contact (using a short list of categories), 5) any onward referral made, and 6) whether any safeguarding concern was raised. Anything more detailed can stay in narrative case notes under T8, which would not be part of the standard attendance sheet.

From the oral health side, A2 is clear on general safeguarding, but I think we should add a short subsection on clinical boundaries for T5. For example, during screening we might notice issues that require urgent follow-up. We need to state that I will not diagnose or prescribe, but will follow the dental clinic supervisor's protocol in A5 for referrals. Also, for consent, we should clarify whether existing dental clinic consent forms cover these outreach screenings or if we need a separate form.

Looking at this from a logistics and data angle, I agree with the minimum fields suggested in M21. For T12 later, we will need consistent IDs and location codes to analyse patterns without exposing personal details. One question: in A2, do we want to specify how long we retain attendance and feedback forms from A3, and who is responsible for secure storage at each site? That might help avoid confusion when we move between schools and community venues.

These are helpful points. On D4, I am comfortable with the list of minimum fields you proposed, as long as we keep the reason for contact categories broad enough to avoid labelling young people in a way that could be stigmatising. I will adjust A2 to reflect that the detailed narrative stays in T8 case notes, and that A3 only captures the agreed minimum. On retention and storage, I will draft a short paragraph specifying retention periods in line with our existing policy and who holds the keys or passwords at each site.

One more suggestion for A2 before we send it up for approval under D3: can we include a simple flow for what happens when a safeguarding concern is raised during a session? For example, 1) immediate safety check, 2) record concern in T8 case notes, 3) inform designated safeguarding lead the same day, 4) agree next steps and record them. That will help staff who are less familiar with social care processes, especially in community locations.

Once you update A2 with these points, I can align A3 and T4 accordingly. For example, I will add a simple tick-box on the attendance sheet to indicate whether a safeguarding concern was raised, without any detail, and a field for the unique ID only. The narrative and follow-up will stay in T8. That should keep the forms easy to use while still giving us enough data for T10 and T12 later.

I like the idea of a simple flow. Could we also add a short note in A2 about how to manage situations where a young person discloses something while we are in a semi-public space, like a corridor near the screening area? Maybe a reminder to move to a more private space as soon as possible and to avoid discussing details within earshot of others. I can also reinforce this verbally when we do the training under T9.

On retention and storage, once you finalise the wording in A2, I can make sure the field visit schedule in A6 and the plan in T6 indicate where physical forms are stored after each session, so they are not left in bags or cars. That will also help us when we collect forms for data entry and analysis.

I have now updated A2 to include: 1) the safeguarding response flow you suggested, 2) the minimum data fields for A3 and T4, 3) a short note on managing disclosures in semi-public spaces, and 4) retention and storage responsibilities. Unless anyone spots a major issue today, I will send A2 and T2 to the social services manager and data and compliance officer for formal review and sign-off under D3.

Thanks for pulling this together. From my side, A2 now covers what we need for the pilot. Once you have the formal sign-off, could you post a short summary in this channel highlighting the key do's and don'ts, especially around consent, disclosures, and record-keeping? That will help ensure everyone has read and understood the procedures before we start sessions.

Once D3 is confirmed, I will finalise A3 and T4 using the agreed minimum fields under D4 and schedule a short walk-through for staff on how to complete the forms correctly. I will also add a brief note at the top of each template reminding staff not to write detailed case information on the attendance sheets.

That will make the later analysis under T12 much cleaner. With consistent fields and clear safeguarding procedures in A2, we should be able to monitor participation and risks through T10 without overcomplicating the paperwork.

threads.thread_goal: Finalise workshop curriculum and oral health session design.

messages.text: I have uploaded a first draft of the Youth Wellbeing Workshop Curriculum Pack in A4, linked to T3. It outlines eight weekly sessions with objectives, suggested activities, and signposting to local support services. Topics include stress and coping, relationships, online safety, and where to get help. This is a starting point, so please review and suggest changes, especially around timing, language, and how it connects with the oral health work in A5.

Thanks for sharing A4. I have also drafted the Oral Health Awareness and Screening Protocol in A5 for T5, with a focus on short, interactive segments that can slot into your sessions or run as stand-alone blocks. It includes a 10-minute talk on everyday oral care, a quick demonstration, and a simple screening checklist. We need to confirm under D6 which activities are realistic within the time you have for each workshop and what we should reserve for separate clinic-based sessions.

I have gone through A4 and it looks strong. For D5, my suggestion is that we keep the eight-session structure but adjust the order slightly to front-load engagement: 1) Welcome and ground rules, 2) Stress and coping, 3) Friendships and relationships, 4) Online life and safety, 5) Health and self-care (including oral health), 6) Managing conflict, 7) Future plans and goals, 8) Review and celebration. That way, we can integrate your oral health content into session 5 and still have flexibility for stand-alone oral health sessions at the clinic.

From a materials perspective, A4 and A5 give us a good base for T7. To keep things accessible, I would like to simplify some of the language and turn key points into short handouts and slides. For example, for the stress and coping session we can have a one-page sheet with three simple strategies and local helpline contacts. For oral health, we can adapt existing clinic leaflets into a youth-friendly format. Once D5 and D6 are agreed, I will finalise the formatting and store everything in a shared folder.

Looking at this alongside T6, I think we should also consider how long each session can realistically run in the school timetable. If we assume 60 minutes, then integrating a 10-minute oral health segment plus activities might be tight on days with assemblies or shortened periods. For D6, maybe we agree that in-school workshops include a short oral health awareness piece only, and we schedule more detailed screenings at the clinic or during dedicated health days.

I agree with that split. For D6, I propose: 1) In-school workshops: 10-minute oral health talk plus a quick Q and A, using a simple visual aid and no clinical screening. 2) Clinic or health day sessions: full screening using the checklist in A5, with follow-up appointments arranged as needed. That keeps us within time and equipment limits and still gives young people a clear route to more detailed care.

I like the revised sequence you suggested in M35. It flows well from building trust to more sensitive topics and then into planning and review. For D5, I am happy to adopt that order in A4. I will also make sure each session plan includes a short check-in and check-out, plus a reminder of support options, so we are not opening up difficult topics without closing them properly.

That sounds workable. To summarise D6: in-school sessions will include a short oral health awareness component only, and more detailed screenings will happen at the clinic or during dedicated health days, following A5. We should also note in A7 and T11 what materials are needed for each type of session so we do not carry unnecessary equipment into schools.

Once D5 and D6 are locked, I will create two sets of youth-facing materials under T7: 1) short handouts and slides for the in-school wellbeing sessions, including the brief oral health segment, and 2) slightly more detailed leaflets for clinic-based screenings. I will keep the design consistent so young people recognise that it is all part of the same pilot.

From a scheduling point of view, the eight-session sequence under D5 fits well into a three-month window if we allow for one or two missed weeks due to exams or holidays. I will reflect the agreed topics and oral health integration in A6 and T6 so schools can see at a glance what is planned each week.

I will update A5 and T5 to clearly separate the in-school awareness component from the clinic-based screening protocol, as per D6. I will also draft the inventory checklist in T11 and A7 to match, so we have one list for school sessions and one for clinic sessions. Once the dental clinic supervisor has reviewed and approved, I will confirm here.

I will now revise A4 to reflect the agreed sequence under D5 and to include a short slot in session 5 for the oral health awareness piece. I will also add notes on group size, suggested room layout, and any materials needed so that T7 and A7 can align easily. Once done, I will send A4 to the social services manager for approval.

Great. Once A4 and A5 are approved, we will be ready to brief youth reps and school staff on the content. I will also make sure that the case note system under T8 and the monitoring under T10 capture which session topic each young person attended, so we can see which themes draw more engagement.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on field visit schedule, logistics, and coordination with schools.

messages.text: I have posted a draft Field Visit Schedule and Location Map in A6, based on the four locations agreed in T1 and the roles we set earlier. This links to T6. The proposal is: 1) Main secondary school on Tuesdays after lunch, 2) Alternative provision on Thursdays mid-morning, 3) Youth drop-in centre on Wednesday early evening every other week, and 4) Clinic-based oral health sessions on Friday afternoons. Please review and flag any clashes or practical issues before we share with schools and the clinic.

Thanks for pulling A6 together. From an outreach perspective, the days look reasonable. My only concern is the Wednesday early evening slot at the youth drop-in centre. Some of the young people we want to reach there have caring responsibilities, so we might need to check with the centre whether a slightly earlier start is possible, or whether a Saturday slot would work better. Also, we should build in time for debrief and case notes after each visit, especially for T8 and T10.

Looking at the school slots, Tuesday after lunch at the main secondary school should be fine for most of the term, but we will need to avoid exam weeks and parents' evenings. Thursday mid-morning at the alternative provision is good, as they tend to have more flexible timetables. When you share A6 with school leadership, could you highlight that we can adjust specific weeks as long as we keep the overall pattern?

From the clinic side, Friday afternoons for oral health sessions are workable, but we need to avoid the first Friday of each month due to existing training. I will check with the dental clinic supervisor and confirm which Fridays we can commit to. Also, for T11 and A7, it would help if A6 indicates which sessions are oral health-focused so I can plan stock checks and equipment transport accordingly.

From an admin and materials angle, the pattern in A6 is clear. To keep T7 and A3 manageable, I suggest we standardise start and end times as much as possible, so staff know when to collect attendance and feedback forms. If we end up with too many variations, it will be harder to track who attended which session, especially at the youth drop-in centre.

Good points. I can adjust the draft in A6 so that the youth drop-in centre slot is shown as a range, for example 4 to 6 pm, and then we can negotiate the exact time with the centre manager. I will also add a 30-minute buffer after each session in T6 for debrief and case notes, so it is visible when we share the schedule with stakeholders.

That works for me. When you send A6 to school leadership and the youth drop-in centre, I am happy to join the conversations to explain the outreach and safeguarding aspects, and to make sure they understand how we will handle consent and follow-up. Once they confirm, we can treat the schedule as locked under D7, with the understanding that we may still move individual weeks around exams or events.

When you speak with school leadership, could you also check whether they prefer the same group of students to attend all eight sessions, or whether they want more open groups where different students can join each week? That will affect how we plan the curriculum in A4 and how we manage attendance in A3.

I have checked with the dental clinic supervisor. We can commit to clinic-based sessions on the second and fourth Fridays of each month during the pilot. I will share these dates with you so you can update A6 and T6. Once that is done and schools have confirmed their slots, I think we will be ready to confirm the overall schedule under D7.

Thanks for confirming the Fridays. I have now updated A6 and T6 with: 1) fixed clinic sessions on the second and fourth Fridays, 2) the school slots with a note about exam weeks, and 3) the youth drop-in centre slot as a flexible early evening range. I will send the draft schedule to school leadership, the youth drop-in centre manager, and the dental clinic supervisor today, copying the social services manager.

Once you have their confirmations, please share the final A6 here. I will then update the headers on the attendance and feedback templates in A3 so that staff can simply tick which site and time slot they are using, rather than writing it out each time.

Quick update: school leadership and the youth drop-in centre manager have now confirmed the proposed slots, with the usual caveat about exam weeks and special events. The dental clinic supervisor has also agreed the second and fourth Fridays. I have uploaded the final version of A6. Unless anyone sees a major issue, I suggest we record this as our agreed weekly outreach schedule under D7.

Agreed. With D7 in place, we can now start sharing the schedule with youth reps and including it in our Monday check-ins. I will also make sure that T1, T8, and T10 reflect the final locations and times, so our mapping, case notes, and weekly monitoring line up with A6.

With the schedule confirmed under D7, I will align T11 and A7 so that stock checks happen two days before each oral health session, whether at school or at the clinic. I will also add a quick pre-session checklist reminder in this channel before each health session.

threads.thread_goal: Review early pilot data, adjust approach, and plan evaluation outputs.

messages.text: We now have the first month of attendance and feedback data compiled in A3, and a short summary of participation and emerging issues from T10. I would like to use this thread to review what we are seeing so far, agree any mid-pilot adjustments, and start sketching what we want to highlight in the final evaluation in A8 under D8. Key headlines from my side: 1) school-based sessions are well attended, 2) youth drop-in centre numbers are lower than expected, and 3) a few safeguarding concerns have been logged and followed up via T8.

I have done an initial pass at the data tables for T12 and shared them in draft form. Early patterns: 1) average attendance at the main secondary school is around 15 per session, with a core group of 10 attending most weeks; 2) the alternative provision has smaller groups but higher consistency; 3) the youth drop-in centre sessions have ranged from 3 to 6 participants. Feedback forms show that young people value the practical activities most. I have noted some limitations in data quality where forms were partially completed.

Building on that, I have added a short note in T12 summarising trends: school sessions are clearly the main driver of reach, while the youth drop-in centre is underperforming relative to our expectations in A1. For D8, we might consider adjusting the schedule in A6 to reduce the number of low-attendance slots and instead add one or two extra clinic-based oral health sessions, where we are seeing good engagement from referrals.

From the oral health side, the clinic-based sessions have been full, with waiting lists on two Fridays. In-school awareness segments have gone smoothly, but we have had to cut questions short a couple of times due to time. For D8, I would support shifting one of the youth drop-in centre slots into an additional clinic session, as long as we keep some outreach presence in the community. That would also make T11 and A7 easier to manage, as we can concentrate equipment in fewer locations.

Qualitatively, the wellbeing workshops feel positive. Young people are engaging well with the stress and coping and relationships sessions, and several have asked for more time on managing conflict. At the youth drop-in centre, the smaller numbers have allowed deeper conversations, but it does raise questions about whether this is the best use of limited time. For D8, I would suggest we keep one monthly session there focused on more intensive support, and reallocate the other slot to strengthen school or clinic-based work.

That aligns with what I am seeing in T10. We have logged a few safeguarding concerns, mostly from school sessions, and follow-up via T8 has been manageable. At the youth drop-in centre, the issues raised have been complex but from a small number of young people. For D8, I propose: 1) reduce youth drop-in centre visits to once a month, focusing on more intensive support and referrals, and 2) add one extra clinic-based oral health session per month, and 3) slightly extend the conflict management session in A4 by trimming some content from another week.

If we go with that adjustment under D8, I will update the attendance and feedback templates in A3 so that we can clearly distinguish between regular and intensive sessions at the youth drop-in centre, and between standard and additional clinic sessions. That will help when we write up A8 and need to show how changes in the model affected participation and outcomes.

I can adjust A6 and T6 accordingly: one monthly youth drop-in centre visit, clearly marked as an intensive support session, and an extra clinic-based slot on one of the remaining Fridays. I will also note this change in T12 so that when we interpret the data we remember that the model shifted mid-pilot.

I am comfortable with that plan. I will update T11 and A7 so that stock checks and equipment prep reflect the new pattern, and I will keep a brief log of any changes in demand at the clinic once the extra sessions start. That will be useful evidence for A8 when we talk about feasibility and resource needs for scaling up.

On the curriculum side, I will tweak A4 so that the conflict management content is expanded slightly, and I will shorten some of the activities in another session to keep within the same overall time. I will also add a short reflection question to the feedback forms, via A3, asking which topics young people would like more of. That should give us richer qualitative input for A8.

I will incorporate that extra reflection question into the feedback template and make sure it is easy to answer quickly. I will also start drafting the structure of A8, with sections on reach, engagement, safeguarding, oral health, and logistics, so we can drop in findings as T10 and T12 progress.

For the evaluation tables in T12, I will add a simple before and after comparison around the mid-pilot adjustment under D8, so we can see whether the changes to A6 and the session mix had any visible effect on attendance and feedback. I will also note any data quality issues so we do not over-interpret small numbers.

To close this out, let us capture D8 clearly: we will 1) reduce youth drop-in centre visits to one intensive session per month, 2) add one extra clinic-based oral health session per month, 3) expand the conflict management content in A4, and 4) update A3, A6, T10, T11, and T12 to reflect these changes and track their impact. These points should form a core part of the learning and recommendations section in A8.
